title: Wet Stock
subtitle: Cyclone Response, Coordination & Pipeline Integrity

brief.userPrompt: Fictional Tropical Cyclone Tevra makes landfall near Beira, Mozambique, on Thursday 11 February 2027 at about 22:00 with winds around 190 km/h and a storm surge; the Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System shows a red alert. The exercise begins at 06:00 on Friday 12 February (Central Africa Time) in the Harbourlight Relief International (HRI) country office in Beira, with Country Director Alberto Matsinhe, Emergency Coordinator Mariam Sesay (arriving from Nairobi at noon), Information Management Officer Naledi Dube, Logistics Manager Joaquim Tembe and Security Focal Point Rui Cossa; headquarters in Geneva is led by Emergency Operations Director Camille Laurent (Crisis Management Team chair). The exercise covers about 72 hours. Timeline and pressure points: by 06:00 61 of 64 staff are accounted for, and the three missing are in Buzi district where communications are down and are found at 11:20; the Beira warehouse roof is damaged and about 20 percent of the stock (3,000 shelter kits, 2,800 jerrycans, 4,000 hygiene kits, 12 portable water treatment units) is wet or missing, so the stock balance and the stock reported to clusters must be corrected; the EN6 crossing at Dondo is cut and Buzi district is reachable only by boat or helicopter; at 08:30 the UN Humanitarian Coordinator holds the first Humanitarian Country Team meeting and requests the activation of clusters for Sofala and Zambezia, with the WASH, health, shelter, food security, protection and logistics clusters meeting daily and the national disaster management agency INGD reporting 412,000 people affected against OCHA's 385,000 (an earlier cut-off); HRI submits its first 3W entries to the clusters by 17:00 and must keep its totals consistent with its situation message and flash update; the WASH cluster gap list shows no partner in Buzi district and shelter uncovered in Nhamatanda, with 12 hours to assign and 48 hours to cover, and HRI decides which gap it can take against its stock, staff, access and funds; the HCT launches a flash appeal of US$ 96 million (WASH 21, health 14, shelter 18, food security 27, protection 6, logistics 7, nutrition 3) and HRI's internal fund releases US$ 350,000; on Friday at 15:00 a container of 6,000 tarpaulins (an emergency shipment through Beira port) is held by customs and demurrage starts on day 5, needing an INGD waiver letter, while the pipeline projects a break for shelter kits within 30 days if no reroute is made; on Saturday a crowd surge at the distribution at the Nhamissa displacement site leads the Security Focal Point to stop movements in the area, share a security alert and decide the level; a WhatsApp rumor says HRI will give cash on Sunday and charge a registration fee; the safeguarding focal point receives a complaint; reports of acute watery diarrhea rise at Nhamissa; the Saving Lives Together framework means the UN security officer receives HRI's alert but is not responsible for HRI staff. Decisions the exercise should record: request for cluster activation, gap assignment, gap covered, escalation of a gap to the HCT, launching or revising the HRI appeal, stopping movements, hibernation or relocation, security alerts shared, family notification, rerouting a shipment, a customs waiver request, public statements. The SimCell plays the UN Humanitarian Coordinator, OCHA, the cluster coordinators, INGD, customs and port officials, donor representatives, other agencies' security focal points, the shipping agent, the community committee at Nhamissa, reporters and the HRI headquarters crisis management team members not played by players.
constraints: Every HRI email address uses the exercise domain harbourlightrelief.example; UN, government and partner contacts use fictional domains on .example; never a real agency, company or media domain.

Humanitarian products follow the formats in the plans: flash updates with the sections situation, needs, response, gaps and constraints, contacts; 3W entries with organization, activity, location at administrative post level, people, dates and funding status; gap lists with the 12-hour assignment and 48-hour coverage targets; every number agrees across the flash update, the 3W and headquarters messages or the difference is explained; security content stays at the decision and communications level (no tactics); times are Central Africa Time.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; the Humanitarian Coordinator, OCHA, cluster coordinators, INGD, customs and port staff, donors, other agencies' security focal points, the community committee, reporters and residents are played by the SimCell.

overview.theme: Duty of care for staff when communications are down, numbers that agree across every product, committing only the stock, staff, access and funds HRI actually has, and safe distributions under crowd and rumour pressure.
overview.threat: Before STARTEX, fictional Tropical Cyclone Tevra made landfall near Beira, Mozambique, at about 22:00 on Thursday 11 February 2027. It brought winds of around 190 km/h and a storm surge, and the Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System showed a red alert. The cyclone damaged the roof of HRI's Beira warehouse, leaving about 20 percent of the prepositioned stock wet or missing. It also cut the EN6 crossing at Dondo, leaving Buzi district reachable only by boat or helicopter with communications down. The exercise opens at 06:00 CAT on Friday 12 February and covers the first 72 hours across Sofala and Zambezia. Pressure points include cluster activation, a US$ 96 million flash appeal, a customs hold at Beira port on 6,000 tarpaulins, and on Saturday a crowd surge, a cash rumour and rising acute watery diarrhoea at the Nhamissa displacement site.
overview.operationalImpact: At 06:00, 61 of 64 staff are accounted for. Three staff members are in Buzi district with no radio or phone contact until they are found at 11:20, and their families are calling the Beira office. The logisticians find that the stock balance (3,000 shelter kits, 2,800 jerrycans, 4,000 hygiene kits and 12 portable water treatment units) is now overstated by about a fifth. The stock already reported to the clusters must be corrected before HRI can commit to any gap. Drivers cannot use the EN6 crossing at Dondo. Field teams for Buzi need boat or helicopter access and a movement approval before they can leave. The Emergency Coordinator does not arrive from Nairobi until noon, so the Country Director carries the first HCT meeting at 08:30 alone. At that meeting, INGD's 412,000 people affected conflicts with OCHA's 385,000. By 17:00 the Information Management Officer must submit the first 3W entries and make them match the situation message to Geneva and the flash update. The WASH cluster gap list shows no partner in Buzi district and shelter uncovered in Nhamatanda, with 12 hours to assign the gaps and 48 hours to cover them. At 15:00 customs hold a container of 6,000 tarpaulins at Beira port. Demurrage starts on day 5, an INGD waiver letter is needed, and the shelter-kit pipeline will break within 30 days unless a shipment is rerouted. On Saturday, displaced families and site managers at Nhamissa face a crowd surge at the distribution, and the Security Focal Point must stop movements in the area and share a security alert. A WhatsApp rumour promising cash on Sunday for a registration fee leads to calls from the community committee and reporters. The safeguarding focal point receives a complaint, and health and WASH staff report rising acute watery diarrhoea at the site.

objectives.name: Duty of Care
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to account for the three out-of-contact staff in Buzi district, report the incident to the Security Focal Point and Country Director within 1 hour, notify the HQ Crisis Management Team chair within 2 hours of activation, and give families only cleared information until the staff are found at 11:20.

objectives.name: Information Integrity
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to correct the overstated Beira warehouse stock balance with the clusters and submit the first 3W entries by 17:00, so that they agree with the situation message to Geneva and the flash update and explain the gap between INGD's 412,000 and OCHA's 385,000 affected.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to decide which WASH and shelter gaps in Buzi and Nhamatanda HRI can take within the 12-hour assignment target, committing only the stock, staff, access and funds it actually has, and to choose between an INGD customs waiver and rerouting a shipment for the held container of 6,000 tarpaulins.

objectives.name: Safe Programming
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to suspend movements and share a security alert without staff names under Saving Lives Together during the Nhamissa crowd surge, while countering the cash-for-registration rumour with one consistent message to the community committee and reporters.

roles.name: Country Director
roles.description: Owns the decision to activate the plan, staff security in Mozambique, commitments up to US$ 150,000 and HRI's position at the 08:30 HCT meeting until the Emergency Coordinator arrives.
standingOrders: Staff First: no programme commitment is made until all 64 staff are accounted for or their status is reported to the HQ CMT.
Commit Only What Exists: offer the clusters only stock, staff and access that the logisticians and Security Focal Point have confirmed.
Notify Upward: tell the Regional Director and the HQ CMT chair within 2 hours of activation, even if facts are still incomplete.
Own the Call: decide on movements and hibernation on the Security Focal Point's advice, and say what the decision means for national staff.

roles.name: Emergency Coordinator
roles.description: Manages the scope and sites of HRI's response from noon on day 1, including the choice of which cluster gaps to take and how distributions at Nhamissa are run.
standingOrders: Gaps With Owners: accept a gap list line only when you can name the owner, the stock and the date it will be covered within 48 hours.
Do No Harm: do not run a distribution at Nhamissa until crowd control, the feedback channel and site safety are in place.
Rumour Response: answer the cash rumour with one cleared message; never promise anything HRI has not funded.

roles.name: Information Management Officer
roles.description: Owns HRI's 3W entries, maps and flash updates, and makes sure the figures match the situation message to Geneva.
standingOrders: One Number: every figure in the 3W, the flash update and the HQ situation message must agree, or the difference must be explained.
Deadline Discipline: submit the 3W to each cluster information manager by 17:00 and correct errors within 24 hours.
Confirmed vs Estimate: label each figure, including the 412,000 versus 385,000 affected, as confirmed or estimated and give its source.
No Double Counting: never add people reached across sectors without saying that the same person may be counted more than once.

roles.name: Logistics Manager
roles.description: Owns the Beira and Dondo warehouses, the fleet and the pipeline, including the recount of wet stock and the customs hold on the tarpaulin container.
standingOrders: Count Before Commit: recount the damaged Beira stock and give the IMO the corrected balance before any gap is pledged.
Pipeline Horizon: report days of stock as stock on hand divided by daily consumption, and flag the shelter-kit break before 30 days.
Waiver or Reroute: seek the INGD waiver letter before demurrage starts on day 5, and prepare a reroute through Nairobi, Dubai or the Logistics Cluster in case it fails.

roles.name: Security Focal Point
roles.description: Manages the security risk assessment, movement approvals, incident reports and security alerts, and advises the Country Director.
standingOrders: One-Hour Rule: report every incident within 1 hour and write the incident report within 24 hours.
Approve Movements: no team goes to Buzi by boat or helicopter, or to Nhamissa during unrest, without a movement approval.
Share Without Names: send alerts to UNDSS under Saving Lives Together saying 'an HRI vehicle', never naming staff, and remember that HRI's security stays HRI's responsibility.

roles.name: Emergency Operations Director (HQ Crisis Management Team Chair)
roles.team: Team F: Headquarters Crisis Management Team Chair
roles.description: Owns the HQ Crisis Management Team in Geneva, its decision log, and the line to the country office, staff families and donors when staff are missing or evacuation is considered.
standingOrders: Take Over When Triggered: activate the CMT once the missing Buzi staff are confirmed out of contact, and keep a timed decision log.
Truth Over Reassurance: give families and donors only facts that the CMT has cleared and checked against the country office.
Support, Don't Override: back the Country Director's in-country decisions unless staff are detained, missing or seriously injured, or evacuation is on the table.

phases.title: Silence from Buzi
phases.goal: Tests whether the Country Director and Security Focal Point account for every staff member after Cyclone Tevra's landfall, act on the out-of-contact report before the facts are confirmed, and meet the 1-hour and 2-hour notification timelines while the Beira warehouse damage comes into view.
beats: (06:00) STARTEX: the GDACS red alert for Tropical Cyclone Tevra and an INGD bulletin confirm landfall near Beira at about 22:00 Thursday with winds near 190 km/h and storm surge. The EN6 crossing at Dondo is reported cut. Staff roll call stands at 61 of 64: three staff in Buzi district have no radio or phone contact.

(06:20) Families of the three Buzi staff call the Beira office asking for news. Players must give only cleared information, report the incident to the Security Focal Point Rui Cossa and the Country Director Alberto Matsinhe within 1 hour, and decide which HMSSSP 3 actions to take at once: stop movements into Buzi and share an alert with the UN security officer and the NGO safety network.

Noise item: a routine fuel invoice query for the Dondo sub-warehouse lands in the Logistics Manager's inbox. At the same time, a Dondo-based driver asks whether to come in to Beira over the EN6 as usual, which is the first schedule-change question.

(07:00) Joaquim Tembe sends a photo from the Beira warehouse at Rua do Porto 18 showing the damaged roof and wet pallets. This is the first sign that about a fifth of the prepositioned stock in HMSCLP 2 is wet or missing, which feeds the 0 to 6 hour stock check in section 4 of the Harbourlight Relief International plan.

The Country Director must notify the HQ Crisis Management Team chair, Emergency Operations Director Camille Laurent in Geneva, within 2 hours of activation and tell the Regional Director Kwame Boateng, with no staff names beyond need-to-know.

phases.title: Numbers That Disagree
phases.goal: Tests whether HRI corrects its overstated stock with the clusters and handles conflicting caseload figures at the first HCT meeting without committing what it does not have, while carrying the Buzi staff search through to resolution.
beats: (08:30) The Country Director, as the NGO platform alternate, attends the first HCT meeting alone because the Emergency Coordinator Mariam Sesay lands from Nairobi only at noon. INGD reports 412,000 people affected and OCHA reports 385,000. The HC asks for HRI's available stock and capacity and signals that cluster activation will be requested.

Under HMSCLP 8, the Logistics Manager's recount shows the stock reported to the clusters (3,000 shelter kits, 2,800 jerrycans, 4,000 hygiene kits and 12 portable water treatment units) is overstated by about 20 percent. The Information Management Officer Naledi Dube must send a corrected 'available' figure that excludes damaged items before any gap commitment.

Red herring (09:40): a community committee member in Buzi tells the office that an 'NGO vehicle was swept off the road'. The report later turns out to concern a private vehicle, which tests whether players pass on unverified information to families or HQ.

A reporter calls the Communications Officer Sofia Machava with a 10:30 deadline asking whether HRI staff are missing in Buzi. The WASH cluster gap list arrives showing no partner in Buzi district and shelter uncovered in Nhamatanda, with the 12-hour assignment clock running.

(11:20) The three Buzi staff are found safe via a Logistics Cluster boat crew. Players must update the families, the CMT chair and the NGO safety network, and decide whether the HMSSSP 3 movement stop and threat level for Buzi still stand.

phases.title: Gaps and the Container
phases.goal: Tests the exercise's one decision point: which Buzi and Nhamatanda gaps HRI commits to within the 12-hour target using only real stock, staff, access and funds, alongside the choice between an INGD customs waiver and rerouting the held tarpaulins.
beats: DECISION POINT (13:00): The WASH cluster asks HRI, as a WASH cluster member, to take the Buzi district WASH gap. Accepting means sending teams by boat or helicopter under the HMSSSP 5 movement authorization into an area the three staff have only just left, and committing scarce water treatment units. Declining leaves Buzi with no partner past the 12-hour assignment target and damages HRI's standing with the cluster. Nhamatanda shelter must be weighed against the corrected shelter kit balance.

Mutual aid: the Logistics Cluster at Beira airport offers shared helicopter slots and boat access. Players must set out who authorizes HRI staff movements (the Country Director at Level 3 under HMSSSP 3) and how HQ CMT oversight fits with the in-country decision now that the Emergency Coordinator has arrived.

(15:00) Customs at Beira port hold a container of 6,000 tarpaulins. Demurrage starts on day 5, an INGD waiver letter is needed, and the shelter-kit pipeline breaks within 30 days. The choice is between pursuing the INGD waiver and rerouting a shipment through the Nairobi hub or Dubai under HMSCLP 4. Players must apply the approval thresholds: an Emergency Coordinator waiver up to US$ 50,000, the Country Director above US$ 50,000, and the Country Director's signing limit of US$ 150,000.

(17:00) The Information Management Officer must submit the first 3W entries at administrative post level. Under SOP-COORD-01 7, they must agree with the situation message to Geneva and flash update no. 1, or explain the 412,000 versus 385,000 difference and the stock correction. The HCT also confirms the US$ 96 million flash appeal, and HRI's request may include only activities that appear in its 3W and costing (SOP-COORD-01 8).

phases.title: Pressure at Nhamissa
phases.goal: Tests safe programming at the Nhamissa displacement site: suspending movements and sharing a nameless security alert during a crowd surge, countering the cash rumour with one message, and steering the 48-hour coverage and pipeline recovery toward a phased return to planned operations.
beats: Time jump to Saturday 13 February (10:00): a crowd surge at the Nhamissa distribution. Under HMSSSP 3, the Security Focal Point must stop movements in the area at once and share a security alert with the UN security officer and the NGO safety network under Saving Lives Together, with no staff names or staff locations in the alert or the flash update. Players must also decide what the change in threat level means for national staff.

A WhatsApp rumour promises cash on Sunday in exchange for a registration fee. The community committee and two reporters call. Players must agree one consistent message across the community committee, the media and the NGO platform. At the same time, the safeguarding focal point receives a complaint that must stay need-to-know.

Health and WASH staff report rising acute watery diarrhoea at Nhamissa. The hurdle: one of the portable water treatment units sent there fails, and the replacement must come from a stock balance that has already been corrected down, which tests whether the 48-hour coverage commitments still hold.

Flash update no. 2 and the updated 3W must reconcile the people reached, the items distributed (net of the Nhamissa suspension) and the tarpaulin pipeline status with the Geneva situation message and the OCHA situation report. HQ CMT and the Regional Director are told how and when HRI will resume.

The Country Director approves a phased restart of Nhamissa distributions, with revised crowd management and a 48-to-72 hour response plan and funding request under section 4 of the Harbourlight Relief International plan, then ENDEX.

msel.event: STARTEX CARD: Tropical Cyclone Tevra made landfall near Beira at about 22:00 on Thursday 11 February 2027. Winds were near 190 km/h and there was a storm surge along the coast. It is now 06:00 Central Africa Time on Friday 12 February 2027, eight hours after landfall, at the HRI country office in Beira. The GDACS event page shows a RED alert for Mozambique. INGD's 05:30 bulletin (Boletim n.º 1, ingd-sofala.example) confirms landfall and widespread flooding, and reports that the EN6 crossing at Dondo is cut. It is overcast with heavy rain bands and gusts of 60–70 km/h, and the rain is easing. Mains power is off across the city and the office is running on its generator. Mobile data comes and goes. HF radio works to Beira and Dondo. The office opened with a skeleton crew of 9 staff on site. Office status is otherwise normal: no injuries reported in Beira and the vehicles are parked in the compound. Roll call board at 05:55: 61 of 64 staff accounted for. Three staff from the Buzi WASH team (a WASH officer, a driver and a community mobiliser) last checked in by radio at 19:40 on Thursday 11 February 2027 from Buzi district. There has been no radio, phone or WhatsApp contact since.
msel.expectedAction: CD decides whether to activate the emergency response plan and starts the 0–6 hour actions: account for every staff member and their dependants, check the office and vehicles, notify HQ and check warehouse stock. SFP treats the Buzi silence as a new threat sign, stops movements to Buzi and shares an alert at once.

hotwash.methodDescription: Ask the room for three things that went well and three things that broke or failed during the first 72 hours after Tevra. Go around the room one team at a time (Country Office leadership, Logistics, Information Management, Programmes and Comms, HQ CMT) so every function speaks, and write each Up and each Down on the whiteboard in that team's words before you discuss any of them.

questions.text: At 0:30 (I-02) the reporter's email about three staff 'swept away' near Buzi reached the Geneva CMT chair and the Beira CD before anyone had confirmed anything. At 0:50 (I-04) UNDSS told you it could only share information and could not promise a seat on the helicopter or the INGD boats. When did you stop waiting for the UN search picture and treat finding your three Buzi staff as HRI's job? Did the Security Focal Point and CD hear within 1 hour, and the CMT chair within 2? And what exactly did you say to the families and to the reporter before the staff turned up at 11:20? Was every line cleared, or were you filling the silence?

At 0:40 (I-03) the storekeeper guessed 'maybe one-fifth' was lost. At 1:20 (I-08) the unsigned recount showed 2,400 usable shelter kits, not 3,000, and the cluster logistics officer was still asking whether he could list all 3,000 for Nhamatanda. How long did the 3,000 figure stay live on the cluster sheet, and who owned the job of correcting it? By 17:00, did your 3W entries, the situation message to Geneva and the flash update all use the same stock figures? Could you explain the gap between INGD's 412,000 and OCHA's 385,000 affected in one sentence that every product used?

At 2:30 (I-15) the WASH cluster asked you to take G-W-01 in Buzi (18,000 people, figure unverified, and the EN6 cut at Dondo) and the Shelter cluster asked about G-S-02 in Nhamatanda (3,500 households). The deadline was 19:30, and declining meant an HCT escalation. When you answered, did you commit only what you actually had: 10 tested water treatment units, not 12, plus real staff, boat or helicopter access and money in hand? Or did the pressure not to leave the line unassigned push you to over-promise? For the 6,000 held tarpaulins, how did you choose between the INGD customs waiver and rerouting, and what information would have let you decide faster?

At 3:18 (I-20) the committee chair read you the '3,000 MT cash, registration costs 150 MT at gate 2' message. Within minutes, Rádio Voz do Centro was going live at 10:30, Diário do Chiveve was asking how many were hurt in the 'stampede', and the NGO platform was asking who runs cash in Nhamissa. Did the committee, the radio reporter and the other NGOs all hear the same single message from you? When did you suspend movements and share the security alert through Saving Lives Together, and did it go out without any staff names?

In the middle of the rumour response, the safeguarding focal point called the EC on a personal line about a man in an HRI vest at registration and asked that the complaint stay with the EC and CD only. How did you keep that complaint confidential while you were also sending public messages and security alerts about the gate 2 'agent'? Did anyone treat the two issues as the same thing before you knew whether they were linked?

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: INGD Sofala provincial delegation duty officer: the host government's disaster management authority and source of the hazard bulletins (Boletim n.º 1 and 2, river levels, road status)
simcellScripts.trigger: A player calls INGD to confirm the Buzi River level or the EN6 crossing at Dondo, to report the three missing staff, to ask for seats on the INGD boats from the Beira fish market quay, to challenge the 412,000 figure, or to ask for the duty waiver letter for container MSKU 448210-3.
hardQuestions: "Boletim n.º 2 says 412,000 affected. Is HRI going to put OCHA's 385,000 in its appeal? The Government's figure is the planning figure. Which one are you using?"

"You want a waiver letter for your container. Send me the written request with the packing list and the declaration. Your declaration says 'shelter materials' and your list says 'tarpaulins and rope'. Which is true? I will not send Foreign Affairs a letter that contradicts customs."
"Seats on our 09:00 boat? These boats are for rescue first. How many people, what are their names, who authorised the trip, and is your request on the Logistics Cluster form? If not, call me back."
"You were working in Buzi on Thursday. Which posts? Are you on the district 3W? I cannot coordinate partners I cannot see."
concessions: Will add the three staff's last known location (Buzi, check-in 19:40 Thursday) to the search picture once the SFP gives a clear description, but promises no rescue tasking.

Will forward the waiver request to Foreign Affairs the same day once HRI gives a signed request whose consignee and description match the packing list. No promise on timing (in line with the MSEL: the letter has still not arrived by Saturday).

Will confirm the road and river status on request: EN6 at Dondo cut for 'at least three days', Buzi River not yet crested. Will accept HRI's Buzi WASH activity into the district picture once it appears in the 3W.

simcellScripts.trigger: The IMO or EC replies to GAP LIST v1 (I-10b) or v2 (I-15), calls to say HRI will or won't take G-W-01 Buzi or G-S-02 Nhamatanda, or the Logistics Cluster stock sheet line for HRI comes up.
hardQuestions: "Your line on the stock sheet says 3,000 shelter kits and 12 water units. Your recount says 2,400 and 10, with 2 untested. Which number do I give the HCT tonight? I am not reporting untested units as coverage."

"You say you take Buzi. Who goes? How many people, which helicopter rotation or boat, and is the movement approved by your security focal point? If they cannot get there before 07:30 Sunday, I have not closed the gap. I have hidden it."
"18,000 people at Buzi post and Estaquinha post. How many does 4 units serve? If you can only do Buzi post, say so in writing and I keep Estaquinha open."
"Assignment target is 19:30 today. If I do not have your email by then, the line goes unassigned to tonight's call and to the HCT on Sunday. Are you sending it or not?"
concessions: Will list HRI as owner of G-W-01 (status 'assigned') only after a written confirmation of units, staff, access route and first service date, as SOP-COORD-01 6 requires.
Will accept partial coverage (for example, Buzi post only) and escalate the rest honestly rather than mark the whole line assigned.

Will update HRI's line on the cluster stock sheet to the signed Recount 1 figures when the Logistics Manager sends them, and will mark the gap 'covered' only after the first service happens and the cluster verifies it.

simcellScripts.trigger: The Logistics Manager or CD calls back about the customs hold (I-14), asks how fast the tarpaulins can be released, asks who pays demurrage, or wants to amend the declaration.
hardQuestions: "Do you have the INGD waiver letter, with a reference number? No? Then customs will not move it before the 3 to 5 working days. Call me when you have the letter."
"The declaration says 'shelter materials'. I can lodge an amended declaration, but I need your signed instruction and the corrected packing list. Who at HRI signs?"
"Demurrage starts Monday, day 5. I need a written instruction and a purchase order number from HRI saying who pays. My company does not carry your charges."
"The terminal is half flooded. If customs inspects tomorrow, can your truck be at the gate within two hours? If it is not, you lose the slot."
concessions: Will lodge the amended declaration within the hour once she receives a signed instruction and a corrected packing list.
Will submit the INGD waiver letter to customs the moment it arrives and ask for a priority inspection slot, estimating 24 to 48 hours after that.
Will ask the shipping line for a demurrage extension once HRI sends the waiver request reference and a written undertaking on charges.

simcellScripts.trigger: The Communications Officer, CD or CMT returns his media slip (I-10 on Friday or I-20 on Saturday), or anyone at HRI calls him to ask him not to run a story.
hardQuestions: "Yes or no: are HRI staff missing in Buzi? A committee man says your car went into the river at Guara-Guara. I have first names from a family. I am live at 10:30. If you will not say, I go with what I have."
"Is the cyclone aid in your port warehouse rotting in the rain? How many kits did you lose? Give me a number."
"Saturday: people say they paid 150 meticais at gate 2 to register for HRI cash. Is HRI charging cyclone victims? Was anyone hurt in the stampede this morning, and how many?"
"Who speaks for HRI, you or Geneva? I need a name and a voice clip by 10:15."
concessions: Will drop the names and use 'three HRI staff' if HRI confirms on the record that all staff are accounted for (once true) and gives a clip before deadline.

Will run HRI's correction of the cash rumour word for word: HRI does not charge for registration and is not paying cash on Sunday, with the feedback line +258 84 555 0188 and the SMS short code. He will only run it if one spokesperson gives it to him before 10:30.
Will report the warehouse damage using HRI's confirmed usable figures instead of 'rotting aid' if HRI gives him the number before deadline.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Sr. Albino Zacarias, chair of the Nhamissa community committee (displacement site, est. 6,800 people)
simcellScripts.trigger: The EC calls back after I-20, HRI tries to send a message to the site about the cash rumour, or HRI discusses the restart proposal from the site manager (I-22).
hardQuestions: "People already paid the man at gate 2. If you say 'no cash', who gives them back their 150 meticais? They will be angry with me, not with you. What exactly do I tell them, and in which words?"
"Your team ran away behind the tent with 388 kits still on the truck. The families who did not get a kit, are they on a list? Who has that list? People say whoever is on the list gets the money."
"Your two mobilisers, Dércio and Luísa, live here. People are asking them. Are they allowed to speak for HRI or not?"
"The committee proposes tokens, two lines, women and older people first, and a complaints desk from 07:00 Sunday. Do you agree, yes or no? I need to announce it today."
concessions: Will read out one HRI message (in Portuguese and the local language) through the committee and the site loudspeaker once HRI gives him the agreed wording, and will point people to the feedback line +258 84 555 0188 and SMS short code.
Will back the token-based restart at 07:00 Sunday and help hand out tokens once HRI confirms who keeps the household list and that it stays need-to-know.

Will pass complaints from families to HRI's feedback line and complaints desk instead of to the press. Concerns about staff conduct go privately to the safeguarding focal point, not through the committee.

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment. Players are judged on how well HRI's plans and coordination arrangements work, not on how well any person or office does.

The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented. Players accept the Tropical Cyclone Tevra situation, the times and the figures on the inject cards as written, even where they differ from current conditions in Beira.

Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures: the HRI emergency response plan, the security plan, the supply chain plan and the HCT coordination SOP. Where a plan is silent, players say what they would do and note the gap for the hot wash.
Players know only what has been delivered to them by inject or by the module narrative. Information held by actors outside the room arrives only when the SimCell delivers it.
Decisions made in one module carry forward. Each time-jump card summarises what happened in between, and players build on those outcomes.
Players may discuss the scenario only with others in the room. They contact real staff, families, partners, donors and media only through the SimCell.
artificialities: Time is compressed. Each module covers one hour of the response in about one hour of discussion. Time-jump cards move the clock between modules, including the overnight jump from Friday 08:00–09:00 to Saturday 09:00.

The SimCell plays everyone outside the room. This includes INGD and the Sofala provincial authorities, UNDSS and the NGO safety network, OCHA and the cluster coordinators, the Logistics Cluster and UNHAS, the weather and hazard authorities (INGD bulletins and GDACS), customs and the clearing agent, families, community committees, reporters, donors and the Nairobi hub.

Systems are named as they appear in the plans but are not used. These include the cluster stock sheet, the 3W, flash updates, HF/VHF radio, satellite phones, the feedback line and the internal emergency fund. Players describe what they would enter or send.

Injects arrive on paper or on screen as cards, emails, radio and phone transcripts, and photographs. Some role holders, such as the Emergency Coordinator while in the air, take part while their real-world counterpart would have no contact.

modules.narrativeMd:
**Module 1: Silence from Buzi (06:00–07:00, Friday 12 February 2027)**

It is 06:00 Central Africa Time in the HRI country office in Beira. Tropical Cyclone Tevra made landfall near Beira at about 22:00 Thursday, with winds near 190 km/h and a storm surge along the coast. The GDACS event page shows a RED alert for Mozambique. INGD's 05:30 bulletin (Boletim n.º 1) confirms widespread flooding and reports that the EN6 crossing at Dondo is cut. Rain is easing, but gusts still reach 60–70 km/h. Mains power is off and the office is running on its generator. Mobile data comes and goes, and HF radio reaches Beira and Dondo. A skeleton crew of 9 staff is on site, and the vehicles are parked in the compound.

The roll call board at 05:55 reads **61 of 64**. Three members of the Buzi WASH team, a WASH officer, a driver and a community mobiliser, last checked in by radio at 19:40 Thursday from Buzi district. There has been no radio, phone or WhatsApp contact with them since. The Beira warehouse at Rua do Porto 18 has not yet reported. During this hour, expect calls from families, from the Dondo base, from the warehouse, from UNDSS and from outside the country.
keyIssues: Acting on the out-of-contact report before the facts are confirmed: stop movements and share the alert at once
Meeting the 1-hour report to the SFP and CD and the 2-hour notification of the HQ CMT chair
What families may be told, and stopping a relative from driving to Buzi himself
Media and diaspora-chat pressure on staff names before HQ has the full picture
Warehouse damage that makes the pre-cyclone stock figures unreliable

**Module 2: Numbers That Disagree (07:00–08:00, Friday 12 February 2027)**

It is 07:00. The rain has eased to showers, but the Buzi River is still rising. The ARA-Centro river bulletin at 06:45 puts the Buzi River at 6.1 m at the Buzi gauge, above the 5.0 m alert level and rising about 0.2 m an hour. INGD's radio bulletin now calls Guara-Guara and Estaquinha in Buzi district 'isolated'. The roll call board still reads **61 of 64**. The Buzi WASH team has been out of contact for 11 hours 20 minutes. UNDSS has added the team's last known location to the search picture. It has said that one UN helicopter is tasked to Buzi and that INGD boats leave the fish market quay at about 09:00, but it has promised no seats. Two families have called back, and one relative is now at the office gate. A wire reporter, the Regional Director and Geneva are all asking for facts.

The UN Humanitarian Coordinator has called the first HCT meeting for 08:30. The Country Director will sit in as the NGO platform alternate because the principal is stuck in Quelimane. The Emergency Coordinator is in the air and cannot be reached until about 11:45. At the Beira warehouse, which lost part of its roof, the storekeeper and two workers have started a pallet-by-pallet recount. The cluster stock sheet still shows Wednesday's pre-cyclone figures under HRI's name. The generator has about 30 hours of diesel left.

**Module 3: Gaps and the Container (08:00–09:00, Friday 12 February 2027)**

It is 08:00. The three Buzi staff have been found alive at the Buzi district administration building and have spoken to the Security Focal Point by satellite phone. The driver has a cleaned cut on his hand. The HRI vehicle is parked on high ground at the Buzi town school. The 'NGO car in the river' turned out to be a private pickup. The roll call board reads **64 of 64 located**: 61 in Beira and Dondo, and 3 in Buzi waiting for transport. A Logistics Cluster boat returns to the fish market quay at about 15:00, but it has two seats, not three.

The HCT meets at 08:30, and the Country Director is attending alone. The Emergency Coordinator lands at about 11:45. Recount 1 has not been signed, and the cluster stock sheet still shows HRI with 3,000 shelter kits 'available'. The WASH cluster's gap list v1 shows two open lines with no partner. Line G-W-01 is safe water and latrines in Buzi for an estimated 18,000 people. Line G-S-02 is shelter kits in Nhamatanda for an estimated 3,500 households. The assignment target is 19:30 today, and the coverage target is 07:30 Sunday. The Buzi River has not crested. INGD now says the EN6 at Dondo will stay cut for at least three days. The generator has about 29 hours of diesel left. Every cluster is asking what HRI can really cover, where, and by when.

**Module 4: Pressure at Nhamissa (09:00–10:00, Saturday 13 February 2027)**

It is 09:00 on Saturday 13 February; the clock has moved forward one day. On Friday the Emergency Coordinator landed at 11:45. The three Buzi staff returned on UNHAS rotation 2 at 12:50. Clusters were activated for Sofala and Zambezia overnight. HRI's 3W went in at 16:52, and Flash Update No. 1 went out at 19:00 using the Recount 1 usable stock. Gap list v3 shows the lines HRI accepted in writing, with a coverage date of 07:30 Sunday. The INGD waiver letter for the tarpaulin container has not arrived, and demurrage starts Monday. The EN6 at Dondo is still cut. The sky is clear and it is 31 °C. Mains power is still off, but 1,200 L of diesel was delivered to the generator.

At 08:00 HRI opened a hygiene kit and jerrycan distribution for 600 households at the Nhamissa displacement site (est. 6,800 people). At 08:40 the line broke. Several hundred people pushed against the fence at the distribution point, and the HRI team withdrew behind the site management tent. Eleven HRI staff are at Nhamissa, nine of them national staff. The roll call board reads **64 of 64 located**. Nobody yet knows what caused the surge.
